cosy-lesson.title: Coffee Drinkers: Fat, Muscle, and Hormones

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Metabolism ≠ Stagnation – the chemical processes that occur within a living organism to maintain life.

p.em: Example: Caffeine temporarily accelerates basal metabolism.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cortisol ≠ Serotonin – a steroid hormone regulating stress responses and metabolism.

p.em: Example: Drinking coffee on an empty stomach can elevate cortisol levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Polyphenol ≠ Pro-oxidant – an antioxidant compound found abundantly in plant foods.

p.em: Example: Coffee is a major dietary source of protective polyphenols.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insulin Sensitivity ≠ Insulin resistance – how responsive cells are to insulin.

p.em: Example: Improved insulin sensitivity aids glucose uptake in muscle tissue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Lipid ≠ Carbohydrate – a class of organic compounds that are fatty acids or insoluble in water.

p.em: Example: Coffee compounds stimulate lipid oxidation during exercise.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bioactive ≠ Inert – having a biological effect on living tissue.

p.em: Example: Bioactive polyphenols exhibit strong anti-inflammatory properties.

cosy-blockquote.p: Endocrine ≠ Exocrine – relating to glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.

p.em: Example: Caffeine interacts with the human endocrine system.

cosy-blockquote.p: Preservation ≠ Degradation – the maintenance of something in its original state or in good condition.

p.em: Example: Lean muscle preservation is crucial during weight loss.

cosy-blockquote.p: Modulation ≠ Disruption – the exertion of a modifying or controlling influence on something.

p.em: Example: Hormonal modulation influences appetite and energy levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Homeostasis ≠ Imbalance – the tendency toward a relatively stable equilibrium between interdependent elements.

p.em: Example: The body continuously strives for metabolic homeostasis.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does caffeine intake affect basal metabolism and lipid oxidation?
★ How many cups of coffee or tea do you drink daily?

Why do endocrinologists study the relationship between coffee consumption and cortisol spikes?
★ Do you feel more stressed or energetic after morning caffeine?

What role do bioactive polyphenols play in improving insulin sensitivity?
★ Are you conscious of antioxidant-rich foods in your diet?

How does coffee consumption support lean muscle mass preservation during caloric deficit?
★ What workout or physical activity routine do you follow?

In what ways does endocrine modulation affect daily metabolic homeostasis?
★ How do you monitor your energy levels throughout the working day?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Could personalized nutrition plans optimize caffeine timing based on individual endocrine profiles?
★ Would you take a genetic test to optimize your daily diet?

Should athletic organizations regulate caffeine as a performance-enhancing bioactive compound?
★ Where do you draw the line between natural supplements and unfair athletic advantages?

How will future bio-hacking trends alter public perception of daily metabolism management?
★ What is your opinion on popular wellness and bio-hacking trends?

Does habitual caffeine usage compromise long-term hormonal homeostasis?
★ Have you ever attempted a caffeine detox?

What public health guidance should be issued regarding cortisol management and morning coffee?
★ What is your ideal morning routine for peak focus?
